newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli tax revenues rose 4.5 pct in first half.
newsitem.headline: Israeli tax revenues rose 4.5 pct in first half.

text.p: The Israeli government's revenues from taxes and fees rose 4.5 percent year-on-year after inflation to 46.3 billion shekels in the first half, the Treasury said on Wednesday.
It added that discounting for changes in tax regulations, the rise was 1.3 percent.

Income and purchase taxes showed a seven percent rise in the first half from a year earlier to 29.2 billion shekels. Income tax revenues alone were about 11 percent higher, mainly due to a 24 percent drop in tax refunds, the Treasury said.
Purchase tax revenues, however, fell 30 percent in the period, which the Treasury attributed to a decline in real estate transactions.
Value-added and customs revenues rose just one percent to 22.5 billion shekels and showed a one percent decline after discounting for changes in rates.

On Tuesday, the Treasury reported a sharp widening in the deficit in June to 3.14 billion shekels, bringing the first-half total to 4.8 billion shekels. The full-year deficit target is 9.7 billion shekels, equal to 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.
The Bank of Israel warned on Wednesday that the June deficit should be taken as a warning to the Treasury to cut spending immediately.
